body.statement: For every finite revealed graph \(G\), an exact branch-safe compiler first evaluates whether \(M_n<n\). If \(M_n\ge n\), it forms none of \(\pi_i(G)\), \(Q_G\), \(w_i(z;G)\), or \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}}\), and returns the all-treated estimator with worst-case MSE at most \(1=\overline U(G)\). If \(M_n<n\), it enumerates the \(n^{k_n}\) ordered seed tuples, groups them by \(Z^{\mathrm{seed}}\), computes every positive \(\pi_i(G)\), every \(w_i(z;G)\), \(Q_G\), and a certified enclosure of \(\lambda_{\max}(Q_G)\), and returns the seed estimator when \(U(G,k_n)\le1\) or the all-treated fallback otherwise, with worst-case MSE at most \(\overline U(G)\). On the high-probability certificate event in Open-ended Question 1, \(\overline U(G_n)\le C_Ur(n,d_n)\).
body.justification: The matched statistical frontier comes with an exact finite procedure that never evaluates an inverse exposure probability outside its positive-probability branch.
body.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Algorithm 4 with Proposition 4.3, gives a polynomial approximation design for its conflict-graph criterion using the imported Partial Vertex Cover 2-approximation in Theorem C.11; it does not provide this branch-safe exact seed-law certificate or close the random-regular GATE minimax gap.
body.consumer: An experimenter can audit the assignment law and worst-case error on the actual revealed network before running the one-shot study.
